Twelve years after Shamba was killed by the wise Prabhasa, Champavati came to Krishna wanting a son.
Champavati saw the sons of Princess Vabhru (Pradyumna and Charudeshna) and desired a similarly powerful, handsome, pure son like Krishna.
Champavati requests Krishna to give her a son who is powerful, invincible, majestic, pure, and like Krishna himself.
Champavati reminds Krishna of his ability to create worlds and how he pleased Shiva (Pashupati) for twelve years to give Princess Vabhru many sons.
Krishna agrees to Champavati's request but asks for time to leave, to which she tells him to go to the ever-victorious Shiva.

The narrator describes the magnificent sights of the incomparable great snow mountain (Mahameru).

attributes.relationship: Upamanyu is a descendant of Vyaghrapada.

extraction_text: The location is praised by gods and Gandharvas and is filled with a pious religious atmosphere.

attributes.details: Includes trees like Tala, Karira, Kadamba, Kakubha, Jujube, Piyala, Rose-apple, Patala, Banyan, Varunaka, Vatsanabha, Pilu, Pine, Monkey-perch, Paryataka, Sal, Tala, Date-palm, Kundu, Punnaga, Ashoka, Mango, and many others.

extraction_text: The trees bear various flowers and fruits, with thickets, shrubs, climbing vines, and bunches of bananas adorning the spaces.

Antelopes, elephants, tigers, lions, leopards, deer, peacocks, snakes, lynxes, buffaloes, and monkeys live together or frequent the area.
Elephants have colorful petals and pollen stuck to their temples, and breezes carry the songs of celestial nymphs (Apsaras), delighting the mind.
The sounds of babbling streams, birdsong, elephant roars, gentle Kinnara songs, and ascetics' chanting blend together.

extraction_text: The inhabitants are great personalities, upholders of Dharma, outstanding among great sages, with spiritual power comparable to blazing fire.
